records.title: Joint Model Partitioning and Bandwidth Allocation for UAV-Assisted Space–Air–Ground–Sea Integrated Network: A Hybrid A3C-PPO Approach

identity_evidence.quote: Received: 28 January 2026 Revised: 14 March 2026 Accepted: 14 March 2026 Published: 18 March 2026

primary_full_report.rationale: This 25-page primary research article formulates joint DNN model partitioning, terminal priority scheduling, and bandwidth allocation via a hybrid A3C-PPO framework evaluated in simulation (Sections 3–5, pp. 5–23).
primary_full_report.quote: Therefore, in this paper, we design a joint optimization framework based on Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (A3C) and proximal policy optimization (PPO).

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Section 5.1 (p. 15) configures three hovering UAVs with four intelligent terminals connected to each UAV, and Section 5.2 p. 21 separately introduces a single-UAV three-terminal Only-PPO component ablation that does not contradict Section 5.1. However, Section 5.2 main hybrid A3C-PPO plots (Figs. 6–7, pp. 19–20) omit simulated UAV counts, 12-terminal totals, and per-UAV results, describe A3C parallelization via worker threads or processes (p. 19), and describe the A3C-PPO-identical environment as four intelligent terminals connected to the UAV (p. 20), leaving actual multi-UAV execution in the main evaluation unconfirmed.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: The experimental environment is configured identically to that of the A3C-PPO framework. Four intelligent terminals are connected to the UAV. Inference tasks are continuously generated by each terminal.

collaborative_inference.rationale: The evaluated DNN workload partitions ResNet18 layer-wise between an intelligent terminal and its nearest associated UAV MEC server (Section 3.1, p. 6; Table 3, p. 17; Eq. 1, p. 7), without modeled inter-UAV partitioning, task migration, or base-station/cloud inference execution despite Figure 1 (p. 6) drawing a three-tier schematic. Section 4.3 (p. 13) assigns one UAV to host a global A3C policy network and remaining UAVs as worker agents for RL coordination alongside Algorithm 1 (p. 15) training updates, but Section 5.2 does not verify runtime inference collaboration or orchestration across a multi-UAV-edge/cloud hierarchy.
collaborative_inference.quote: During deployment, one UAV serves as the central node hosting the global policy network for coordinated decision-making, while the remaining UAVs act as worker agents responsible for local state collection and policy sampling.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Section 5.2 (pp. 16–23) provides simulation evaluations of ResNet18 cut-point latencies (Table 3, Figs. 3–4), PPO vs. random and brute-force partitioning (Fig. 5), A3C-PPO vs. AC-PPO and DDPG-PPO convergence (Fig. 6), Only-A3C/Only-PPO ablations (pp. 20–21, Figs. 7–8), learning rates (Fig. 9), and terminal priority scheduling (Fig. 10).
evaluative_evidence.quote: The effectiveness of the proposed A3C-PPO hybrid architecture is verified through comparative experiments. Two baseline strategies are constructed for evaluation. The bandwidth allocation strategy based on A3C is denoted as Only-A3C.
